name: Attention and Filtering
summary: Your senses deliver millions of bits per second, but consciousness handles only a tiny fraction. Attention is the brain's spotlight.
description: The prefrontal cortex and posterior parietal cortex form the brain's top-down attention network. They send feedback signals to sensory areas, amplifying relevant neural activity and suppressing irrelevant input. The salience network (anchored in the anterior insula and anterior cingulate cortex) monitors for unexpected, emotionally significant, or potentially dangerous stimuli — the bottom-up attention system. This filtering explains inattentional blindness — you can look directly at something and not see it if your attention is focused elsewhere.
